messages.content:
"You probably mean lib.matplotlib.axis.Axis.get_offset_text(self). It looks like:
```python
1157 :     def get_offset_text(self):
1158 :         """Return the axis offsetText as a Text instance."""
1159 :         return self.offsetText
```"

The test `test_offset_text_visible()` checks whether the visibility of the y-axis offset text is correctly set in an axes object. However, the test fails with an AssertionError because the get_visible() method of the offset text returns True instead of False.

Following the execution path, we find that the get_offset_text() method of the Axis class (in lib.matplotlib.axis) returns a Text instance representing the axis offsetText. This Text instance is created in the __init__ method of the Axis class and its visibility is initially set to True. In the test, the y-axis tick parameters are modified such that label1On is False and label2On is True, which indicates that there should be no visible offset text (label1On=False), but this doesn't seem to have any effect on the Text instance's visibility.

Consequently, un-expected behavior of the get_visible() method is observed, leading to the error demonstrated by the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
